key_insight: Residual learning becomes far more sample-efficient when it uses directional task-error feedback and an informative prior together, enabling stable real-robot juggling with very few failures.
engineering_relevance: For robot control and skill refinement, the paper shows that using task-specific error signals can outperform sparse scalar rewards and improve convergence on real hardware.
method: Directional task-error supervision instead of only scalar reward
Task error model used to select informative rollouts
Fixed-Jacobian Newton-style residual updates compared against Bayesian optimization and stochastic search
evidence_signal: On Barrett WAM arms, the system achieved stable three-, four-, and five-ball juggling, typically converging from the second attempt after an initial drop, with task error then decreasing monotonically.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the task-error model and prior structure, so convergence speed may degrade if the analytic prior is badly misaligned or joint tracking is poor.
paper_title: Task-Error Residual Learning for Real-Robot Five-Ball Juggling
